title: Add lib/features/auth/ and core/providers/firebase_providers.dart to no_firebase_outside_core's whitelist per Rule 3

evidence.quote:
if (path.contains('lib/core/auth/')) return true;
    if (path.contains('lib/core/sync/')) return true;

why: Three enforcement artifacts for the same rule disagree. docs/coding-standards.md Rule 3 and root Makefile audit check 6 (for firebase_auth) both authorize THREE directories, explicitly including `lib/features/auth/`. Root Makefile check 11 (for cloud_firestore/firebase_storage) and this custom_lint rule (for all three Firebase packages, uniformly) only authorize TWO. Concretely and currently: `lib/core/providers/firebase_providers.dart` — the exact file coding-standards.md Rule 3 names as the sanctioned Firebase-injection point, and which does `import 'package:firebase_storage/firebase_storage.dart'` directly — sits at `lib/core/providers/`, outside both `core/auth/` and `core/sync/`. This custom_lint rule would flag that canonical, standards-compliant file as a Rule-3 violation the moment custom_lint is unbricked; only the fact that custom_lint is currently broken is hiding this.
recommendation: Add an explicit exemption for `lib/core/providers/firebase_providers.dart` (matching Makefile check 11's own extra exclusion) and decide whether `lib/features/auth/` should be whitelisted too (it doesn't exist yet, but the doc promises it will be exempt) — then make coding-standards.md Rule 3, both Makefile checks 6 and 11, and this rule agree on the same directory set.
acceptance_criteria: no_firebase_outside_core_test.dart gains a case asserting firebase_providers.dart (or its path pattern) is allowed.
Rule 3's authorized-directory list is identical across docs/coding-standards.md, no_firebase_outside_core.dart, and Makefile checks 6 and 11.
